slot.brief: Compare rms speeds of two gases at possibly different temperatures; find the ratio using v_rms ∝ √(T/M) with mole data given.

stem: A vessel contains $2$ mol of neon at $600$ K, while another contains $5$ mol of argon at $400$ K. Given their molar masses as $20$ g mol$^{-1}$ and $40$ g mol$^{-1}$, respectively, find the ratio of their rms speeds, $v_{\text{Ne}}:v_{\text{Ar}}$.

verdicts.working: Using v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M), the ratio is sqrt((600/20)/(400/40)) = sqrt(3):1.

working:
$v_{\text{rms}}\propto\sqrt{T/M}$
$\dfrac{v_{\text{Ne}}}{v_{\text{Ar}}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{600/20}{400/40}}=\sqrt{3}$

Independent check: Using v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M), the ratio is sqrt((600/20)/(400/40)) = sqrt(3):1.
